reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue revolves around whether behavioral constructs like sHR can be considered valid scientific constructs. A scientific construct must represent the joint, unitary action of independent variables. If these variables fail to act as a unit—such as when one variable’s effect cancels another’s—then the construct cannot be treated quantitatively. Habit strength (H_s) is shown to depend on multiple antecedent conditions, each contributing differently. When these variables interact, their combined effect may produce identical behavioral outcomes regardless of individual variation. This leads to non-uniqueness in H_s, undermining its status as a reliable construct. The validity of such constructs hinges on empirical testing of variable synergy. Without such validation, constructs remain speculative. Thus, the failure mode lies in assuming unitarity without verifying it through controlled experiments.
